title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Improved health sector efficiency, governance, and drug safety

At least 50% reduction of the number of illegal, counterfeit, substandard, or not quality-assured drugs on the market in 2016 from 26% in 2007 Progress/Status: Prevalence of counterfeit, substandard and illegal drug Survey was conducted in 2013. Survey results reveal 19% of unregistered and 14% of substandard drugs in the market. As a result of the Survey on “Prevalence of substandard, unregistered and falsified medicines in Mongolia”, in 2017, it was reduced to 4.3% of unregistered drugs and 10.1%- substandard medicines in the market. Data Source: Study using the standard WHO methodology Actual value:

A transparent public reporting system on hospital performances and drug safety is in place Progress/Status: Since 2014, the "Health Indicators" - the annual report of the MOHS includes a chapter on "Pharmaceutical sector indicators". Assessment of Public reporting system on hospital performance includes main performance 9, safety 3, patient satisfaction related output indicators were accepted by the MOH; and Centre for Health Development (CHD) is responsible coordination and implementation of the PRS in the health sector. Data Source: Ministerial order (MOH) Base year: 2010 Baseline value: N

Road map to establish 10 additional general hospitals by 2020 approved by 2016 Progress/Status: Hospital care development policy (2014-2023) was approved by MOH order No.55, 2014. Mid-term implementation strategy (2015-2019) was approved by MOH order No.181, 2015. The implementation strategy was published in 2015. In 2017, the MOH integrated these two documents and some other policy papers into one document named “State Policy on Health” (2017). Road map to establish 5 additional general hospitals approved in Health sector master plan (2020-2026) by 2020. Data Source: Cabinet decree and national conference report Base year: 2010 Baseline value: N
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 2.2. Hospital management module integrated in a local training institution Indicator: 50 managers have undergone short-term management training in a local management school (sex disaggregated). Progress/Status: Completed. Training curricula and handbooks are developed and being used by national training institutes since 2014. In total, 54 managers (61% of females) were trained in two rounds of hospital management training in 2015. Data Source: PIU reports Actual value:

Output: 3.4. Implementation of good manufacturing practice (GMP) Indicator: At least five local drug manufacturers certified by upgraded GMP standard Progress/Status: Completed. A regular assessment had been conducted in 5 most promising local drug manufacturers since 2012 to support them to be certified by the upgraded GMP standard. The IVICO and Monos Pharma companies were certified by upgraded GMP standards in Feb 2015, then Nahia and Enkhiin shuuder companies obtained GMP certificates in 2017, and Tsombo LLC in 2019. Data Source: Certification reports (MOH/Drug Agency)
Actual value:

Output: Component 1: Strengthened Hospital Services in Ulaanbaatar 1.1. Hospital development policy and strategic plan for Ulaanbaatar Indicator: At least 30% of members of working groups on the strategic plan are female Progress/Status: Working groups established since 2011 consistently have over 50% female participation and it is increased to 61.6% as of Q2 2021. Data Source: Ministerial order (MOH) Actual value:

Output: 3.2. Strengthened drug regulatory functions Indicator: More than 80% of regulatory functions (registration, inspection, laboratory, GMP) score positive (Baseline review 2011, verification 2015) Progress/Status: Completed. A baseline review of drug regulatory functions was undertaken in 2011.The score of the drug regulation in Mongolia was 46.9%. The review of 2015 shows an increased score for drug regulation at 57%. The DRA was established and operational for all regulatory functions since January 2021 and an increased score for drug regulation is at 80%. Data Source: WHO data collection tool for the review of drug regulatory systems Actual value:

Output: 11. Strengthened post-marketing surveillance and adverse drug reaction monitoring Indicator: 90% of drug committees reporting quarterly by 2013 from 50% in 2009 (reporting irregularly) Progress/Status: Completed. Ministerial order on procedures on reporting on adverse drug reaction (ADR) is approved in 2013. The National Pharmacovigilance strategy is approved by MOHS ministerial order in 2014. Trainings for medical professionals and for hospital drug therapeutic committees were conducted in 2013-2014. The number of reported ADRs has increased 4-times since 2010. Data Source: Quarterly reports (in 2009 50% of the 40 hospitals reported randomly)
Actual value:

Output: 1.2. A hospital capital investment planning system is established and operational Indicator: Regulatory framework for capital investment planning system established Progress/Status: Regulation on medical equipment inventory system and its use was approved by MOH Ministerial order 493 in Dec 2017. Data Source: Ministerial order (MOH) Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2012 Target value: Y

Output: 1.3. A demonstration multifunctional general hospital established in Songinohairkhan district Indicator: A hospital system established with a surgery unit and an additional specialty (preferably obstetrics and gynecology); linked outpatient and inpatient department Progress/Status: Completed. Concept Design and Functional Plan for the new hospital, approved by MOH in 2014. Architectural design of the hospital developed and approved by the National Construction Development Center in Oct 2015. The bidding process completed in May 2017. MOH signed a contract with Vamed Engineering, the contractor, on 24 May 2017. In November 2018, the government requested an additional financing to address cost overruns caused by (i) government new regulations introduced during implementation of the ongoing project (e.g., new requirements for seismic resistance, upgraded national standards for hospital construction); (ii) limited restructuring of the building to answer address requests made by nearby residents; (iii) construction of a separate building to house the hospital electrical substation and medical gas container, which were originally planned to be located in the basement of the hospital, to conform with requirement of the government inspection authority; (iv) variations in quantities and volumes from the initial bill of quantities; and (v) additional costs to re-route the hospital access road due to the decision of the government to retain the existing hospital. In 2019 ADB approved the additional financing of $16.0 million to complete the construction. The hospital construction completed and commissioned in November 2020 by the state expertise. The medical and non-medical equipments supplied and accepted by MOH's technical working group for inspection of equipment. The installation and calibration of the medical and non-medical equipment were completed in Q1 2021. The hospital building was handed over to the end-user in early April 2021.
Data Source: PIU reports
Hospital report/district management Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 1.3. A demonstration multifunctional general hospital established in Songinohairkhan district Indicator: Patient satisfaction increased (survey data disaggregated by gender) Progress/Status: Almost completed. Patient satisfaction survey was conducted in 2014. Survey results revealed that in average 4.94±1.67 percent of patients are “less satisfied” with service they received, 68.8 percent thinks that hospital' diagnostic and treatment equipment and tools needed to be improved, and 21.5 percent would like to have improved attitude and communication of medical staff toward patients. The final survey (Patient satisfaction survey and Community sore card evaluation) was conducted in Dec 2020, and a qualitative part of the survey was also conducted. The survey report is developed and submitted to the MOH in May 2021. Data Source: Patient satisfaction surveys undertaken semiannually Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 1.4. Increased hospital governance Indicator: Gender-specific needs for services and diagnostic requirements identified Progress/Status: Completed. Gender-specific needs for services and diagnostic requirements identified for SHD demonstration hospital and reflected in the Functional plan of the hospital in 2014. The specific gynecological and obstetric needs of disabled women were included in an updated version in 2019.
Data Source: Project report
Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2016 Target value: Y

Output: 1.4. Increased hospital governance Indicator: Hospital licensing based on needs (certificates), minimum number of beds, and services and diagnostic requirements operational Progress/Status: Completed. Two ministerial orders were approved in 2013 to improve hospital licensing based on consultant' recommendations. These are (i) MOHS ministerial order no.143 on terms of references and working principles of the licensing committee of the MOHS; (ii) ministerial order no.145 on licensing regulations, and procedures. Data Source: State legislation (Parliament)
Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2014 Target value: Y

Output: 1.4. Increased hospital governance Indicator: Hospital performances available to public Progress/Status: Completed. The public reporting on hospital performance was developed and pilot tested in 3 hospitals. Decision of MOH to institutionalize the public reporting system at demonstration Songinokhairkhan hospital was issued in November 2020. Data Source: Ministerial order (MOH)
Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2013 Target value: Y

Output: 12. Strengthened drug safety governance function at MOH Indicator: Annual feedback and corrective action reports by 2014 Progress/Status: Completed. In 2014, the Drug regulatory unit of the NCHD responded with 27 feedback recommendation letters to 20 public and private hospitals and 7 feedback letters were sent to pharmaceutical wholesale and retail companies. Data Source: Annual reports
Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2014 Target value: Y

Output: 12. Strengthened drug safety governance function at MOH Indicator: Annual overview of drug safety indicators and achievements by 2013 Progress/Status: Completed. Drug safety indicators are included in the NMP implementation plan. The plan was approved by the ministerial order in Dec 2014. Annual report with indicators was developed and approved by Management Board in 2015 and publications were printed in 2015, 2016, 2017, and 2018.
Data Source: Annual report, WHO indicators website (indicators from WHO drug policy indicator guide) Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2013 Target value: Y

Output: 12. Strengthened drug safety governance function at MOH Indicator: MOH public information on drug safety including rapid alert system improved by 2014 (data on persons affected by unsafe drugs are sex-disaggregated) Progress/Status: Completed. A web-based software program (LICEMED) to provide public information on products (registered medicines), suppliers (licensed wholesale companies, manufactories, and pharmacies), professionals (licensed), and processes (issued license), including rapid alert system warning on unregistered or counterfeit drugs and data on persons affected by unsafe drugs, was upgraded and approved in Nov 2015 and copyrighted in 2017. The system is operational. Data Source: MOH public information on drug safety including rapid alert system improved by 2014 (data on persons affected by unsafe drugs are sex-disaggregated) Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2014 Target value: Y

Output: 2.2. Hospital management module integrated in a local training institution Indicator: Report identifying and addressing constraints to achieving gender balance in senior hospital management Progress/Status: this indicator was removed based on recommendation of the Midterm review mission Data Source: PIU reports Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2014 Target value: Y

Output: 3.3. Upgraded drug control laboratory, including accreditation system Indicator: ISO-17025 certificate awarded to the drug control laboratory Progress/Status: Completed. Drug Control Laboratory building has been upgraded with the support of PRC grant in 2013; new equipment were installed in November 2013. Pre audit for Medicines and bio preparation laboratory was provided by International accreditation body- ANAB ACLASS in May 2015. Final audit was organized in Oct 2015 and ISO-17025 certificate by international accreditation body was awarded to the DCL in Dec.2015. Data Source: ISO-appointed authorized body
Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 3.3. Upgraded drug control laboratory, including accreditation system Indicator: Laboratory accreditation system approved by MOH Progress/Status: this indicator has been removed based on recommendation of the Midterm review mission Data Source: Ministerial order (MOH)
Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2014 Target value: Y

Output: 3.4. Implementation of good manufacturing practice (GMP) Indicator: GMP guidelines and inspectorate under GASI upgraded to PIC/S standard Progress/Status: Completed. A new national GMP standard (MNS5524:2014) was approved by the Mongolian Agency for Standardization and Metrology in 2014. A GMP certification procedure was approved by MOHS in 2013. Data Source: Expert evaluation report
Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2014 Target value: Y

Hospital care development policy is approved by Ministerial Order no.55, 2014. Mid-term implementation strategy is approved by ministerial order no.181, 2015.Mid-term implementation strategy (2015-2019) is approved by MOH order No.181, 2015. Data Source: Ministerial order (MOH) Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2012 Target value: Y

Output: Component 2: Strengthened Human Resource Development 2.1. Strengthened postgraduate specialist structure and residency programs Indicator: Four specialist curricula brought up to international standards, including gynecology-obstetrics Progress/Status: Completed. Curricula in four clinical areas (internal medicine, general surgery, obstetrics-gynecology and pediatrics) were revised in 2014 and approved by respective professional boards and associations (Dec 2015), and by MOH Order #A/172, 07 Dec 2016. The revised residency training curriculum was piloted at MNUMS during the academic years between 2016 and 2019. Postgraduate training curricula for nurses was also revised and approved by the Nursing professional board. Data Source: PIU reports
Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2014 Target value: Y

Output: Component 2: Strengthened Human Resource Development 2.1. Strengthened postgraduate specialist structure and residency programs Indicator: Institutional plan that sets out a framework for organizations involved in policy development, planning, accreditation, and training of specialists developed Progress/Status: Completed. Institutional plan developed. Legal changes pertaining reforming of postgraduate medical specialist training system reflected in the new Law on medical care and services, approved by the parliament in May 2016. Data Source: Cabinet decree
Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2013 Target value: Y

Output: Component 3: Strengthened Drug Safety Regime 3.1. A drug regulatory authority established Indicator: Institutional development plan of the Drug Regulatory Agency approved and implemented Progress/Status: Completed. The concept of establishment of a drug regulatory authority as an integrated authority with strengthened regulatory functions and improved coordination and quality of medicine is incorporated in several policy documents: (i) Government Action plan 2012-2016; (ii) National Medicines Policy, approved by parliament in October 2014; and (iii) the law on medicines and medical devises was revised in Aug 2020. The government issued decision to establish a Drug Regulatory Agency in November 2020. evelopment of the MOHS. Core regulatory functions of the unit are: (i) registration of medicines and medical devises, (ii) licensing of specialists and providers, (iii) issuance of import and export licenses, (iv) monitoring and reporting adverse drug reactions, (v) monitoring medicines marketing and advertisement, (vi) promoting rational use of medicines, (vii) developing national pharmacopeia and standards. But some functions are still with the General Agency for State Inspection (GASI) such as drug control and control and inspection. Data Source: Ministerial order of MOH approving development plan Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2013 Target value: Y

Output: Component 3: Strengthened Drug Safety Regime 3.1. A drug regulatory authority established Indicator: Trainee participant lists are disaggregated by gender throughout the duration of the project Progress/Status: Completed. In total of 1492 people (82.9% female participants) participated in 25 different types of professional trainings for MOHS, GASI staff and for pharmaceutical companies. Data Source: Annual report of the DRA Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2016 Target value: Y
